correctness.rationale: The two-step line flag has block sizes \((1,a,b)\) and dimension \(N=ab+a+b\). For the natural polarization, the dominant weight is \(\omega_1+\omega_{a+1}\). Evaluating the positive-root leading coefficient of the Weyl dimension formula gives the displayed exact degree. The Schubert affine-cell decomposition gives Euler characteristic \((a+b+1)!/(a!b!)\). After division, exact cancellation gives coordinate growth ratios for \(R=D/E\). Each numerator factor is strictly larger than its matched denominator factor for \(a,b\ge1\), so \(R\) increases strictly from \(R(1,1)=1\). The bundled checker independently matches the root-product and factorial degree formulas and replays the ratio identities.

value.rationale: Both invariants are canonical for the same homogeneous variety: Euler characteristic counts its affine Schubert cells, while the Segre–Pluecker degree counts generic complementary hyperplane intersections in its natural minimal product embedding. The theorem gives a complete, sharp comparison across the entire two-parameter line-flag family and isolates a unique equality at the smallest complete flag. The monotone quotient provides a reusable benchmark for comparing enumerative complexity with Schubert-cell complexity beyond ordinary Grassmannians.
